clusters.summary: quoteIdentifierIfNecessary(vars[0]) is called with undefined when the SQL expression has no sibling query, so isValidIdentifier's toUpperCase throws a TypeError and the editor crashes on render where it previously rendered 'FROM undefined'.
clusters.rationale: With refIds empty vars[0] is undefined and isValidIdentifier calls identifier.toUpperCase() → TypeError during render, where it previously rendered 'FROM undefined'; exactly thread 0.

clusters.summary: The alerting DAG's cleanTableName strips quotes and parens but not backticks and truncates at the first space, so backtick-quoted FROM targets no longer match any refId, Graph.link throws, and the SQL expression is dropped from the alert graph.
clusters.rationale: cleanTableName strips only ['"()] and splits at the first space, so the now-default `FROM \`gdp per capita\`` yields target "`gdp", Graph.link throws for a nonexistent node, and createDAGFromQueriesSafe rejects the SQL expression; the PR generates such queries by default (alerting refIds are renamable) without fixing the DAG parser.

clusters.summary: Core feature code imports quoteIdentifierIfNecessary from the decoupled mysql datasource plugin workspace, coupling core to a plugin internal in the wrong dependency direction.
clusters.rationale: mysql is a decoupled plugin workspace (own package.json/webpack config, listed under grafana/decoupled-plugins-overrides) and no other core code imports from it; core depending on a plugin internal is a real but small dependency-direction concern, not blocked by lint.

clusters.summary: The two new test files fail the repo's CI lint gates: @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any and import/order errors plus prettier --check failures from trailing whitespace and formatting.
clusters.rationale: Verified: both test files carry trailing-whitespace lines (prettier), use `as any` under @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any: 'error', and metaSqlExpr.test.ts lacks the required blank line between parent and sibling import groups — real CI lint failures, but mechanical.

clusters.summary: quoteIdentifierIfNecessary wraps identifiers in backticks without doubling embedded backticks, so a refId like a`b yields malformed SQL.
clusters.rationale: Correct that the helper wraps without escaping embedded backticks so a refId containing ` yields malformed SQL; real but an extreme edge case in a pre-existing helper.

clusters.summary: The `refId.label || refId.value || ''` fallback in the completion provider can hand quoteIdentifierIfNecessary an empty string, producing a completion of two bare backticks (reachable only if a refId has neither label nor value).
clusters.rationale: Technically true, but ExpressionQueryEditor always sets value/label to q.refId so a refId with neither is unreachable in practice.

clusters.summary: metaSqlExpr.ts binds to a file-local regex-only quoteIdentifierIfNecessary with no reserved-word check while the other call sites use the mysql helper, so reserved-word refIds are quoted in the editor but left bare in the metadata query, which fails and silently empties column autocomplete.
clusters.rationale: metaSqlExpr.ts binds to a file-local regex-only quoteIdentifierIfNecessary (no reserved-word check) while SqlExpr/completion use the mysql helper, so a reserved-word refId is quoted in the editor but bare in the metadata query — precisely thread 2.

clusters.summary: The read-back path never unquotes: Monaco tokenizes a backtick-quoted table name into separate tokens so getTableToken yields a lone backtick or quoted name, which fetchSQLFields re-quotes into broken SQL and whose refId filter matches nothing, so column autocomplete silently returns empty for the very refIds this change enables.
clusters.rationale: Monaco's mysql grammar emits the backtick as its own identifier.quote token, getTableToken returns it, fetchSQLFields re-quotes it and its refId filter matches nothing so column completion returns []; this is the production read-back defect thread 7 describes (quoted query.table vs raw refId lookup).

clusters.summary: The second completion-provider test wraps all assertions in `if (resolveFunc)` with no expect(resolveFunc).toBeDefined() backstop (and checks only name, not completion), so it can pass with zero assertions and does not protect the changed line.
clusters.rationale: Verified: the second test has no expect(resolveFunc).toBeDefined() before the if-guard and asserts only name, so it can pass vacuously and does not exercise the changed completion line — a correct small test-quality nit.

clusters.summary: plugin-ui appends the ' $0' cursor tab stop only when completion === name, so backtick-quoted table completions lose the trailing placeholder — a cosmetic UX inconsistency.
clusters.rationale: Verified: insertText appends ' $0' only when completion === name, so quoted completions lose the trailing space/tab stop — a cosmetic difference in a third-party helper, not worth reviewer attention.

clusters.summary: The GenAI suggestion/explain path still passes raw unquoted refIds to the model, so generated SQL for space-containing refIds remains unquoted and fails.
clusters.rationale: SqlQueryActions receives refIds={vars} (raw refId.value) and the prompt injects them unquoted with no quoting instruction, so the GenAI surface is left outside the fix; whether generated SQL actually fails depends on the model, so this is a follow-up gap rather than a verified defect.

clusters.summary: The third metaSqlExpr test asserts field-name quoting at metaSqlExpr.ts:29 that predates the diff — characterization of existing behavior, not a regression test for the fix.
clusters.rationale: True that line 29's field-name quoting predates the diff so the third test is characterization, but adding such a test is harmless and not actionable.

clusters.summary: The /g flag on the isValidIdentifier regex .test() looked like a lastIndex carry-over trap, but the literal is re-evaluated per call so each test starts fresh — refuted.
clusters.rationale: Self-refuted note; the regex literal is re-created per call so lastIndex does not carry over.

clusters.summary: The new tests leave the currently-broken paths uncovered: no case for empty refIds, a reserved-word refId, or an already-quoted table on the read-back path.
clusters.rationale: Composite missing-tests note; its already-quoted-table read-back case is thread 7's requested regression test (and the empty-refIds case is thread 0's), so it restates gaps humans raised.

clusters.summary: SqlExpr.tsx derives the table name from refId.value while the completion provider uses refId.label || refId.value; both callers set them equal so it is only a latent inconsistency.
clusters.rationale: Self-described latent inconsistency with no observable effect since the only caller sets label === value.

clusters.summary: Because initialQuery is now quoted it no longer equals previously-saved spaced-refId expressions, so GenAISQLSuggestionsButton shows 'Improve query' instead of 'Generate suggestion' for them — judged not a real defect.
clusters.rationale: True label change for previously-saved (broken) unquoted initial queries, but self-declared not a defect — a cleared note.

clusters.summary: Considered whether the Go backend rejects backticked table names; refuted — the vitess parser takes the unquoted TableName.Name so backticked refIds resolve server-side.
clusters.rationale: Considered-and-cleared note asserting no defect; TablesList records tableName.Name.String(), which the vitess parser yields without backticks, so backticked identifiers resolve server-side as stated.

clusters.summary: Considered whether metaSqlExpr.test.ts's mocks diverge from the real modules; verified they match and the assertions would fail if quoting were removed.
clusters.rationale: Considered-and-cleared note asserting no defect.

clusters.summary: The new SqlExpr test reads onChange.mock.calls[0][0] after only waiting for onChange to be called; the mount-only effect is the sole reachable caller so calls[0] is unambiguous and matches the sibling test's convention.
clusters.rationale: A considered-and-cleared note asserting no defect.

clusters.summary: `refIds.map((v) => v.value!)` uses a non-null assertion that hides the undefined-vars[0] case from the type checker; the line is outside the diff.
clusters.rationale: Without the `!`, vars would be (string|undefined)[] and quoteIdentifierIfNecessary(vars[0]) would not type-check, so the assertion is what let the crash-prone call compile; but the real undefined comes from an empty array (no noUncheckedIndexedAccess), so the causal framing is loose and the line predates the diff.

clusters.summary: The RESERVED_WORDS list is MySQL 8.0.31's while the SQL expression engine is vitess/go-mysql-server, so any word vitess reserves that MySQL does not would be left unquoted — unverified dialect mismatch.
clusters.rationale: Unverified speculation about a dialect mismatch with no concrete offending word identified; the pre-existing MySQL keyword list is a reasonable choice for a go-mysql-server/vitess backend.

clusters.summary: If Monaco auto-closes a typed backtick, inserting an already-backticked completion could produce doubled backticks — unverified, depends on the editor's language configuration.
clusters.rationale: The editor uses Monaco's mysql language configuration whose autoClosingPairs are {}, [], (), ", ' — no backtick pair — so a typed backtick is not auto-closed and the doubled-backtick scenario does not arise.

clusters.summary: The metaSqlExpr test asserts the queries.filter argument with expect.anything(), which matches [] and so passes whether or not the refId lookup succeeded.
clusters.rationale: The third argument is asserted with expect.anything(), which matches [] so a failed refId lookup goes unnoticed — the same gap thread 7 raises about the source-query lookup in fetchSQLFields being untested.

clusters.summary: Considered whether the first completion-provider test's `if (resolveFunc)` guard could pass vacuously; it is preceded by expect(resolveFunc).toBeDefined() at line 15, so it cannot.
clusters.rationale: Considered-and-cleared note asserting no defect.

clusters.summary: Recommends an integration-level test driving the real path (initial query text → editor token → fetchSQLFields) rather than unit tests that feed each stage idealized input.
clusters.rationale: Its complaint that the unit tests feed each stage idealized input (queries[].refId equal to query.table) instead of the real editor→fetchSQLFields path is thread 7's substance, phrased as a generic recommendation.

clusters.summary: metaSqlExpr.test.ts's uuid v4 mock is not load-bearing because the assertion uses expect.objectContaining and never checks refId — dead setup.
clusters.rationale: True that expect.objectContaining never checks refId so the uuid mock is unused by any assertion, but dead test setup is not worth a reviewer's attention.
